items.text: Career Advice Hub How to become a data analyst in Australia in 2027 By a staff writer 8 minute read Data analyst roles remain one of the most common entry points into a technology career. In this guide we explain what the job involves, what employers ask for, and how to apply successfully. What does a data analyst do? Typical responsibilities include cleaning data, building reports and dashboards, and explaining results to non-technical colleagues. Common requirements Most job ads ask for SQL, a visualisation tool such as Power BI or Tableau, and sometimes Python. Qualifications Many analysts hold a degree in commerce, IT or statistics, but bootcamps and short courses are increasingly accepted. How to apply Build two or three portfolio projects using public data, write a short summary of each, and tailor your resume to each ad. Salary Graduate analysts in Sydney typically earn between $70,000 and $85,000. Related articles Ten interview questions for analysts. How to write a cover letter. Subscribe to our newsletter.

Business News Tech hiring slows as employers favour contractors By a business reporter 10 November 2026 Advertised technology vacancies fell for the third month in a row in October, according to figures from a fictional recruitment industry body, as employers paused permanent hiring and turned to contractors for short projects. Recruiters said graduate programs were still running but with fewer places, and that candidates with cloud and data skills continued to receive multiple offers. One recruiter said employers were taking longer to make decisions and were asking for more interview rounds than a year ago. Economists expect demand to recover in the first half of next year as interest rates ease. The body's chief executive said the slowdown was concentrated in startups and that government and banking roles held steady. Readers looking for work were advised to keep their skills current and to apply widely. Related coverage Interest rates on hold. Startups cut costs. Share this article.

items.text: GradGuide Graduate program applications 2027: a step-by-step guide Updated November 2026 Most large employers open graduate program applications between February and April. This guide walks you through each stage, from online application to assessment centre. Step 1 Check eligibility requirements: many programs require Australian citizenship or permanent residency, and some require you to have finished your degree within the last two years. Step 2 Research the responsibilities of each rotation so you can explain why you want them. Step 3 Prepare for online tests: numerical, verbal and situational judgement. Step 4 The video interview: practise answering in under two minutes. Step 5 Assessment centre: group exercise, case study and partner interview. When to apply Apply early; some programs review applications as they arrive. What employers look for Teamwork, curiosity and clear communication matter more than a perfect grade average. Read next How to answer behavioural interview questions.
